item.title: IShowSpeed unveils ambitious Africa livestream tour that could redefine global creator travel content
item.description: IShowSpeed is officially heading to Africa. On Sunday morning (Dec. 21), the 20-year-old streamer announced his Speed Does Africa Tour, where he’ll be streaming through the continent in a trip that spans a whopping 20 countries in 28 days.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Gaming For Good: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan hosts girls’ rights livestream; fans see her most authentic side
item.description: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan is bringing her Twitch community and activism together through Gaming for Good: A Livestream for Girls’ Rights. The actor will host her signature chatty stream alongside youth leaders and advocates from around the world, encouraging viewers to support Plan International Canada’s Gifts of Hope while keeping her platform positive, authentic, and free from hate.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner pitches $112bn plan to turn Gaza rubble into a tech hub
item.description: Jared Kushner unveiled a $112 billion plan to transform Gaza into a tech and tourism hub, featuring high-speed rail and luxury resorts. The proposal, presented to regional governments, relies on US funding and Hamas disarmament, a condition analysts deem unlikely. Significant physical reconstruction challenges also loom large over this ambitious, yet uncertain, vision.

item.title: Is Vivek Ramaswamy an anchor baby? What does the term mean?
item.description: Far-right activist Nick Fuentes labeled Vivek Ramaswamy an 'anchor baby,' sparking debate. The term, widely considered derogatory, refers to children born in the U.S. to undocumented parents, allegedly to secure family immigration. Ramaswamy, born in Ohio to legally immigrated parents, does not fit this definition, highlighting the term's use as a political slur amid ongoing immigration discussions. Read more here!
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK man sentenced to 5 years in jail for biting off a guest’s finger at best friend’s wedding
item.description: A UK man, Daniel Peasnell, received a five-year prison sentence for biting off a guest's fingertip at his friend's wedding. The 33-year-old, who had been drinking heavily, attacked Stephen Dixon when he intervened to restrain him. The judge condemned Peasnell's actions as 'behaving like a wild animal,' using his teeth as a weapon. Dixon's finger required partial amputation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Pranita Venkatesh: Indian-origin psychologist who just became San Carlos’ youngest mayor
item.description: San Carlos, California, has a new mayor, Pranita Venkatesh, a child psychologist of Indo-Fiji diaspora. Sworn in on December 8, 2025, she is among the city's youngest leaders and a prominent voice for South Asian representation. Venkatesh plans to focus on public safety, childcare, economic stability, infrastructure, and affordable housing, aiming to connect community needs with effective governance. Read more here!

item.title: Top 10 US states with the highest median household income: Leading states, key industries, and economic insights
item.description: Massachusetts leads the US with a $104,828 median household income, fueled by its educated workforce and strong tech and biotech sectors. New Jersey, Maryland, and Hawaii also rank high, showcasing diverse economies from finance to tourism. These states attract talent and investment, though high living costs are a common factor.

item.title: Why did Lamarr Wilson commit suicide? Inside the heartbreaking loss of the tech YouTuber who inspired millions
item.description: Lamarr Wilson, a well known Los Angeles based tech and lifestyle YouTuber with over 2.11 million subscribers, has died by suicide at 48. His death was confirmed by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner and a family member. Tributes from Geoff Keighley and fans highlight Wilson’s lasting impact on the tech and creator community.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Candace Owens shares shocking fresh witness claim about Erika Kirk meeting security before Charlie Kirk death
item.description: Candace Owens shared claims from a former special forces witness who says he saw Erika Kirk and security chief Brian Harpole at Fort Huachuca before Charlie Kirk’s reported death. The claims were made on Owens’ podcast and remain unverified. No police or federal agency has confirmed the account so far.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: ‘We have a country to fix’: As MAGA feuds escalate, Harmeet Dhillon urges conservatives back to policy
item.description: Senior conservative lawyer Harmeet Dhillon urged right-wing influencers to cease public feuds and focus on policy and governance, citing a country needing fixing. Amidst MAGA-aligned disputes over ideology and leadership, Dhillon's call for unity was supported by some but challenged by others who believe airing grievances is crucial for confronting extreme ideas within the movement.

item.title: The Watchlist: Why It's a Wonderful Life is the perfect movie to restore your faith in humanity
item.description: A late-night viewing of 'It's a Wonderful Life' offered unexpected solace and a profound reminder of life's value. The film beautifully portrays George Bailey's selfless nature and his struggle with perceived failure. Through a guardian angel's intervention, George realizes the immense impact of his quiet sacrifices, highlighting the significance of every life and the power of gratitude.
item.dc:creator: Sneha

item.title: ‘In my heart I knew...’: Andrew Tate breaks silence on why he lost to Chase DeMoor in Dubai boxing match
item.description: In a highly publicized boxing match in Dubai, Andrew Tate faced off against Chase DeMoor but ultimately fell short. Though he started off strong, Tate's endurance waned, resulting in a majority decision loss. Acknowledging the challenge and his age, he congratulated DeMoor, recognizing him as a formidable champion.
